mn8:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.
mn8:2.1: Then when it was evening, the venerable Mahā Cunda rose from meditation, and he went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said:
mn8:3.1: ‘Venerable sir, (there are) these various views that arise in the world
mn8:3.2: associated either with self-doctrines or with world-doctrines:
mn8:3.3: (now) does the abandoning and relinquishing of such views come about in a bhikkhu who is giving attention only to the beginning?’
mn8:3.4: ‘There are, Cunda, these various views that arise in the world
mn8:3.5: associated either with self-doctrine or with world-doctrine:
mn8:3.6: (Now) whatever (the basis) those views arise on, whatever they underlie, whatever they are exercised on, when a man sees (that basis) as it actually is with right understanding thus: “This is not mine, this is not I, this is not myself”, then in that way comes about in him the abandoning of such views, and likewise the relinquishment of them.
mn8:4.1: ‘It is possible here that secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unprofitable dhammas, some bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the first jhāna which is accompanied by initial application and sustained application, with happiness and pleasure born of seclusion.
mn8:4.4: But it is not these (attainments) that are called “effacement” in the Noble One’s discipline:
mn8:4.5: these are called “a pleasant abiding here and now” in the Noble One’s discipline.
mn8:5.1: ‘It is possible here that with the stilling of initial and sustained application, some bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the second jhāna which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without initial and sustained application, with happiness and pleasure born of concentration.
mn8:5.4: But it is not these (attainments) that are called “effacement” in the Noble One’s discipline:
mn8:5.5: these are called “a pleasant abiding here and now” in the Noble One’s discipline.
mn8:6.1: ‘It is possible here that with the fading as well of happiness some bhikkhu abides in equanimity, and mindful and fully aware, still feeling pleasure with the body, he enters upon and abides in the third jhāna on account of which Noble Ones announce: “He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful”.
mn8:6.4: But it is not these (attainments) that are called “effacement” in the Noble One’s discipline:
mn8:6.5: these are called “a pleasant abiding here and now” in the Noble One’s discipline.
mn8:7.1: ‘It is possible here that with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, some bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.
mn8:7.4: But it is not these (attainments) that are called “effacement” in the Noble One’s discipline:
mn8:7.5: these are called “a pleasant abiding here and now” in the Noble One’s discipline.
mn8:8.1: ‘It is possible here that with complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with disappearance of perceptions of resistance, with non-attention to perceptions of difference, (aware that) “space is infinite”, some bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the base consiting of the infinity of space.
mn8:8.4: But it is not these attainments that are called “effacement” in the Noble One’s discipline:
mn8:8.5: these are called “quiet abidings” in the Noble One’s discipline.
mn8:9.1: ‘It is possible here that by completely surmounting the base consisting of the infinity of space, (aware that) “consciousness is infinite”, some bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the base consisting of the infinity of consciousness.
mn8:9.5: “quiet abidings” in the Noble One’s discipline.
mn8:10.1: ‘It is possible here that by completely surmounting the base consisting of the infinity of consciousness, (aware that) “there is nothing”, some bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the base consisting of nothingness.
mn8:10.5: these are called “quiet abidings” in the Noble One’s discipline.
mn8:11.1: ‘It it possible here that by completely surmounting the base consisting of nothingness, some bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
mn8:11.4: But these (attainments) are not called “effacement” in the Noble One’s discipline;
mn8:11.5: these are called “quiet abidings” in the Noble One’s discipline.
mn8:12.1: ‘Now, Cunda, here is where effacement can be effected:
mn8:12.2: ‘1. Others will be cruel; we shall not be cruel here: effacement can be effected thus.
mn8:12.3: ‘2. Others will kill living beings; we shall abstain from killing living beings here: effacement can be effected thus.
mn8:12.4: ‘3. Others will take what is not given; we shall abstain from taking what is not given here: effacement …
mn8:12.5: ‘4. Others will not live the life divine; we shall live the life divine here: effacement …
mn8:12.6: ‘5. Others will speak falsehood; we shall abstain from flase speech here: effacement …
mn8:12.7: ‘6. Others will speak maliciously; we shall abstain from malicious speech here: effacement …
mn8:12.8: ‘7. Others will speak harshly; we shall abstain from harsh speech here: effacement …
mn8:12.9: ‘8. Others will gossip; we shall abstain from gossip here: effacement …
mn8:12.10: ‘9. Others will be covetous; we shall be uncovetous here: effacement …
mn8:12.11: ‘10. Others will have a mind of ill-will; we shall have no mind of ill-will here: effacement …
mn8:12.12: ‘11. Others will have wrong view; we shall have right views here: effacement …
mn8:12.13: ‘12. Others will have wrong intention; we shall have right intention here: effacement …
mn8:12.14: ‘13. Others will have wrong speech; we shall have right speech here: effacement …
mn8:12.15: ‘14. Others will have wrong action; we shall have right action here: effacement …
mn8:12.16: ‘15. Others will have wrong livelihood; we shall have right livelihood here: effacement …
mn8:12.17: ‘16. Others will have wrong effort; we shall have right effort here: effacement …
mn8:12.18: ‘17. Others will have wrong mindfulness; we shall have right mindfulness here: effacement …
mn8:12.19: ‘18. Others will have wrong concentration; we shall have right concentration here: effacement …
mn8:12.20: ‘19. Others will have wrong knowledge; we shall have right knowledge here: effacement …
mn8:12.21: ‘20. Others will have wrong deliverance; we shall have right deliverance here: effacement …
mn8:12.22: ‘21. Others will be obsessed by sleepiness and drowsiness; we shall be free from sleepiness and drowsiness here: effacement …
mn8:12.23: ‘22. Others will be agitated, we shall not be agitated here: effacement …
mn8:12.24: ‘23. Others will be uncertain; we shall get beyond uncertainty here: effacement …
mn8:12.25: ‘24. Others will be angry; we shall not be angry here: effacement …
mn8:12.26: ‘25. Others will be inimical; we shall be without enmity here: effacement …
mn8:12.27: ‘26. Others will be contemptuous; we shall not be contemptuous here: effacement …
mn8:12.28: ‘27. Others will be domineering; we shall not be domineering here: effacement …
mn8:12.29: ‘28. Others will be envious; we shall not be envious here: effacement …
mn8:12.30: ‘29. Others will be avaricious; we shall not be avaricious here: effacement …
mn8:12.31: ‘30. Others will be fraudulent; we shall not be fraudulent here: effacement …
mn8:12.32: ‘31. Others will be deceitful; we shall not be deceitful here: effacement …
mn8:12.33: ‘32. Others will be obdurate; we shall not be obdurate here: effacement …
mn8:12.34: ‘33. Others will be haughty; we shall not be haughty here: effacement …
mn8:12.35: ‘34. Others will be difficult to admonish; we shall be easy to admonish here: effacement …
mn8:12.36: ‘35. Others will have bad friends; we shall have good friends here: effacement …
mn8:12.37: ‘36. Others will be negligent; we shall be diligent here: effacement …
mn8:12.38: ‘37. Others will be faithless; we shall be faithful here: effacement …
mn8:12.39: ‘38. Others will be conscienceless; we shall be conscience-minded here: effacement can be effected thus.
mn8:12.40: ‘39. Others will be shameless; we shall have shame here: effacement can be effected thus.
mn8:12.41: ‘40. Others will be of little learning; we shall be of great learning here: effacement …
mn8:12.42: ‘41. Others will be idle; we shall have aroused energy here: effacement …
mn8:12.43: ‘42. Others will be unmindful; we shall have established mindfulness here: effacement …
mn8:12.44: ‘43. Others will have poor understanding; we shall possess understanding here: effacement can be effected thus.
mn8:12.45: ‘44. Others will misapprehend according to their individual views, hold on (to them) tenaciously and relinquish (them) with difficulty; we shall not misapprehend according to individual views, shall not hold on tenaciously, and shall relinquish with ease: effacement can be effected thus.
mn8:13.1: ‘Cunda, I say that even the arising of mind in profitable dhammas is of great importance, so what should be said of bodily and verbal operations consequent thereupon? Therefore, Cunda:
mn8:13.2: ‘1. Mind should be aroused thus: Others will be cruel; we shall not be cruel here.
mn8:13.3: ‘2. Mind should be aroused thus: Others will kill living beings; we shall not kill living beings here. ‘3-43 … ’
mn8:13.4: ‘44. Mind should be aroused thus: Others will misapprehend according to individual views, hold on (to them) tenaciously and relinquish (them) with difficulty; we shall not misapprehend according to individual views, shall not hold on tenaciously, and shall relinquish with ease.
mn8:14.1: ‘Cunda, suppose there were an uneven path and another even path by which to avoid it;
mn8:14.2: and suppose there were an uneven ford and another even ford by which to avoid it, so too:
mn8:14.3: ‘1. A person given to cruelty has non-cruelty by which to avoid it. ‘2. One given to killing living beings has abstention from killing living beings by which to avoid it. ‘3. One given to taking what is not given has abstention from taking what is not given by which to avoid it. ‘4. One given to what is not the life divine has the life divine by which to avoid it. ‘5. One given to false speech has abstention from false speech by which to avoid it. ‘6. One given to malicious speech has abstention from malicious speech by which to avoid it. ‘7. One given to harsh speech has abstention from harsh speech by which to avoid it. ‘8. One given to gossip has abstention from gossip by which to avoid it. ‘9. One given to covetousness has uncovetousness by which to avoid it. ‘10. One given to a mind of ill-will has non-ill-will by which to avoid it.
mn8:14.4: ‘11. One given to wrong view has right view by which to avoid it. ‘12. One given to wrong intention has right intention by which to avoid it. ‘13. One given to wrong speech has right speech by which to avoid it. ‘14. One given to wrong action has right action by which to avoid it. ‘15. One given to wrong livelihood has right livelihood by which to avoid it. ‘16. One given to wrong effort has right effort by which to avoid it. ‘17. One given to wrong mindfulness has right mindfulness by which to avoid it. ‘18. One given to wrong concentration has right concentration by which to avoid it. ‘19. One given to wrong knowledge has right knowledge by which to avoid it. ‘20. One given to wrong deliverance has right deliverance by which to avoid it.
mn8:14.5: ‘21. One obsessed by sluggishness and drowsiness has freedom from sluggishness ane drowsiness by which to avoid it. ‘22. One given to distraction has non-distraction by which to avoid it. ‘23. One given to uncertainty has the state of having got beyond uncertainty by which to avoid it. ‘24. One given to anger has non-anger by which to avoidit. ‘25. One given to enmity has non-enmity by which to avoid it. ‘26. One given to contempt has non-contempt by which to avoid it. ‘27. One given to domineering has non-domineering by which to avoid it. ‘28. One given to envy has non-envy by which to avoid it. ‘29. One given to avarice has non-avarice by which to avoid it. ‘30. One given to fraud has non-fraud by which to avoid it. ‘31. One given to deceit has non-deceit by which to avoid it. ‘32. One given to obduracy has non-obduracy by which to avoid it. ‘33. One given to haughtiness has non-haughtiness by which to avoid it. ‘34. One given to difficulty of admonishment has ease of admonishment by which to avoid it ‘35. One given to making bad friends has making good friends by which to avoid it. ‘36. One given to negligence has diligence by which to avoid it. ‘37. One given to faithlessness has faith by which to avoid it. ‘38. One given to lack of conscience has conscience by which to avoid it. ‘39. One given to shamelessness has shame by which to avoidit. ‘40. One given to little learning has great learning by which to avoid it. ‘41. One given to idleness has aroused energy by which to avoid it. ‘42. One given to forgetfulness has establishment of mindfulness by which to avoid it. ‘43. One given to lack of understanding has perfection of understanding by which to avoid it. ‘44. One given to misapprehension according to individual views, to holding on (to them) tenaciously, and to difficulty in relinquishing them, has not misapprehending according to individual views, not holding on tenaciously, and ease in relinquishment, by which to avoid it.
mn8:15.1: ‘Cunda, just as no matter what unprofitable dhammas there are, they all lead to a lower state; and just as, no matter what profitable dhammas there are, they all lead to a higher state, so too:
mn8:15.2: ‘1. A person given to cruelty has non-cruelty as a higher state. ‘2. One given to killing living beings has abstention from killing living beings as a higher state. ‘3-43 ...
mn8:15.3: ‘44. One given to misapprehension according to individual views, to holding on (to them) tenaciously, and to difficulty in relinquishing (them), has not misapprehending according to individual views, not holding on tenaciously, and ease in relinquishing, as a higher state.
mn8:16.1: ‘Cunda, that one who is himself floundering in a slough should pull out another who is floundering in the slough is not possible;
mn8:16.2: that one who is not himself floundering in a slough should pull out another who is floundering in the slough is possible;
mn8:16.3: that one who is himself untamed, undisciplined, and unattained to Nibbāna, should tame another, discipline him, and lead him to Nibbāna, is not possible;
mn8:16.4: that one who is himself tamed, disciplined and attained to Nibbāna should tame another, discipline him and lead him to Nibbāna, is possible. So too:
mn8:16.5: ‘1. A person given to cruelty has non-cruelty by which to attain Nibbāna. ‘2. One given to killing living beings by which to attain Nibbāna.
mn8:16.47: ‘44. One given to misapprehension according to individual views, to holding on (to them) tenaciously, and to difficulty in relinquishing (them), has, not misapprehending according to individual views, not holding on tenaciously, ease in relinquishing, by which to attain Nibbāna.
mn8:17.1: ‘So, Cunda, the way of effacement has been shown by me, the way of arising of mind has been shown by me, the way of avoidance has been shown by me, the way of the higher state has been shown by me, and the way of Nibbāna has been shown by me.
mn8:17.2: ‘What should be done for his disciples out of pity by a Master who seeks their welfare and has pity (on them), that I have done for you, Cunda.
mn8:17.3: There are these roots of trees, these empty huts. Develop jhāna, Cunda, do not delay, lest you later regret it. This is our message for you.’
mn8:17.4: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn8:17.5: The venerable Mahā Cunda was satisfied, and he delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
